title: Micron pulls the plug on future 4F^2 DRAM
gist: A SemiWiki forum post relaying a Tom's Hardware report says Micron has concluded after about two decades that 4F2 DRAM cells offer no meaningful density advantage and add cost and complexity, even as Samsung and SK hynix keep 4F2 on their roadmaps. Micron CTO Scott DeBoer argues capacitor dimensions and pitch, not transistor area, set cell density.

insights.claim: Micron has concluded after roughly two decades of work that 4F2 DRAM cells offer no meaningful density advantages, increase manufacturing complexity and costs, and have fundamental scaling limitations.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Removes 4F2 from Micron's roadmap, a divergence from rivals' DRAM scaling path.
insights.locator: Micron pulls the plug on future 4F² DRAM

insights.claim: 4F2 DRAM cells have long been seen as a holy grail because they promise to cut cell area by 33% versus conventional 6F2 designs.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Explains why the technology is a closely watched scaling lever.
insights.locator: DRAM featuring 4F² memory cells has long been considered

insights.claim: Micron's Scott DeBoer said the company invented 4F2 DRAM and has evaluated it over the past two decades but not pursued it because of increased complexity and cost.
insights.speaker: Scott DeBoer
insights.so_what: Direct management statement; Micron is not just delaying but declining the path.
insights.locator: Micron invented 4F² DRAM," said Scott DeBoer

insights.claim: Samsung and SK hynix still have 4F2 memory cells in their roadmaps, according to TechInsights, so Micron's rejection puts it on a unique trajectory.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: If Micron is right, rivals may spend on a path with limited payoff; if wrong, Micron lags in density.
insights.locator: Interestingly, both Samsung and SK hynix

insights.claim: Micron previously delayed integrating EUV lithography contrary to its rivals and still retained competitive cost and performance positions, making the 4F2 skip not completely surprising.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Micron has a track record of contrarian process choices that worked out.
insights.locator: Several years ago, the company delayed integration of EUV

themes.theme: Why density gains do not materialize

insights.claim: DeBoer explained that the dimensions and pitch of DRAM capacitors, rather than the nominal area of transistors, ultimately determine how many cells fit on a wafer, because both 4F2 and 6F2 transistor structures must fit beneath the capacitors.
insights.speaker: Scott DeBoer
insights.so_what: Capacitor scaling, not transistor shrink, is the DRAM density bottleneck to track.

insights.claim: Micron believes 4F2 adds manufacturing steps and complexity that raise cost without delivering sufficient benefits.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Cost-per-bit matters more than theoretical cell area.
